evidence.positive: Against the running instance (port 53375, build 10f82fe08) fetched the shell at / and extracted the hashed assets it references: /static/index.WYelJArk.js, /static/index.Cr8zYOMI.css, /static/rolldown-runtime.CdcebO_E.js. GET /static/index.WYelJArk.js with Accept-Encoding: gzip returned 200, content-encoding: gzip, cache-control: max-age=2592000, immutable, vary includes accept-encoding, 574,183 bytes on the wire (2,017,593 without Accept-Encoding). GET /static/index.Cr8zYOMI.css likewise returned gzip + max-age=2592000, immutable, 60,006 bytes on the wire (449,689 identity). Then drove headless Chromium via Playwright with a CDP Network session: launch 1 of /app-launch fetched all three assets from the network (fromDiskCache=false); launch 2 in the same browser context reported fromDiskCache=true, encodedDataLength=0 for the script, the runtime chunk and the stylesheet, i.e. no bytes transferred. Simulated a deploy between launch 2 and launch 3 by copying the bundle to /static/index.LOOPDEPLOY.js inside the container and re-pointing /app/resources/static/index.html at it: launch 3 re-fetched the shell (no-store) and requested /static/index.LOOPDEPLOY.js from the network (fromDiskCache=false, content-encoding gzip, immutable) while the unchanged css and runtime chunk stayed fromDiskCache=true. Reverted index.html (md5 c1bb86bc… matches the backup) and removed the probe file; /static/index.LOOPDEPLOY.js now 404s.
evidence.negative: GET /index.html returned cache-control: no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate with pragma: no-cache and expires: 0 (gzipped, since text/html is in the compression list). GET /app-launch returned 200 with the same no-store headers and the shell body (2303 bytes), so a launch always re-reads the shell. Non-bundle paths kept Spring Security's no-store: /favicon.ico (image/x-icon, no content-encoding, no-store), /api/version (403, no-store), and a missing /static/does-not-exist.js (404 JSON, no-store), so the immutable header is only stamped on hashed assets that actually resolve. The 1,268-byte /static/rolldown-runtime.CdcebO_E.js was served immutable but identity-encoded, which is Spring's default 2 KB min-response-size threshold rather than a gap.
evidence.red_check: Backed up /app/classes/com/guided/orci/configuration/StaticAssetCacheConfiguration.class (md5 d5218fa104cb733ae8d878f83559bead) and /app/resources/application.yml (md5 f5ed851321cb2ca5004a27983520a74a) out of the container. Compiled a pre-fix-shaped StaticAssetCacheConfiguration (addResourceHandlers registers nothing, logs one WARN line via slf4j) against the container's spring-webmvc 7.0.9 jars, copied it over the shipped class, and sed'd server.compression.enabled to false in the container's application.yml, then docker restart. After readiness the log showed 'RED CHECK OR-3106: pre-fix StaticAssetCacheConfiguration active, /static/** registered without immutable Cache-Control' and the same probes went red: GET /static/index.WYelJArk.js with Accept-Encoding: gzip came back with NO content-encoding, content-length 2017593 (full 2.0 MB on the wire) and cache-control: no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate; the stylesheet likewise 449689 bytes, no-store. Restored both files from the backups, confirmed md5s match (d5218fa1… and f5ed8513…, enabled: true back in the yml), restarted, and re-ran the positive probes: gzip + max-age=2592000, immutable on both assets again, index.html still no-store. The swap loaded cleanly (the class is additive config, nothing else depends on it), so the data flip was not needed.

red_check_signature: RED CHECK OR-3106: pre-fix StaticAssetCacheConfiguration active, /static/** registered without immutable Cache-Control
caveats: Header behaviour produces no organic log line, so the red-check signature is a WARN line emitted by the swapped pre-fix class itself; the red observation is the header/byte-count change on the probes.

The acceptance criteria name dev; this exercised the local Docker build of main directly against Tomcat, so anything in front of dev (ALB/CloudFront) that strips or adds Content-Encoding or Cache-Control was not in the path.

Chunks under Spring's default 2 KB compression threshold (rolldown-runtime.CdcebO_E.js, 1.3 KB) are served immutable but identity-encoded; ENV-005 only checks the main bundle so this does not affect it.
The deploy simulation re-pointed the shell on the live filesystem rather than rolling a new image; it proves index.html is re-read and a new hash is fetched, not the ECS rollout itself.

automation.assessment: Existing coverage is solid for the core: StaticAssetCacheConfigurationTest (MockMvc) locks in immutable on /static and /audio, no-store on /index.html and the /app-launch forward; ENV-005 (@core smoke) checks the deployed main bundle for content-encoding gzip and the immutable Cache-Control. Gaps worth locking in are the stylesheet (ENV-005 only resolves the .js), the no-store on the shell at the smoke level (the deploy-takes-effect half of the ticket is only covered in MockMvc), and the browser-level second-launch cache hit that the ticket's second acceptance criterion actually describes.
proposed_tests: ENV-006 (@core, environment-health.spec.ts): the stylesheet referenced by the shell is served with content-encoding gzip and cache-control max-age=2592000, immutable.
ENV-007 (@core, environment-health.spec.ts): GET /app-launch and GET /index.html carry cache-control no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate, so a deploy is picked up on the next launch.

ENV-008 (@supplemental, environment-health.spec.ts): in one browser context load /app-launch twice and assert via a CDP Network session that the script and stylesheet responses on the second load report fromDiskCache=true with zero encodedDataLength.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: The hashed script and stylesheet are served gzipped with Cache-Control max-age=2592000, immutable, and a second Chromium launch loaded both from disk cache with zero bytes transferred.
Negative: index.html, /app-launch, favicons and API responses keep no-store, and a simulated deploy that re-pointed the shell at a new bundle hash was fetched from the network on the next launch.
Red check: Swapping in a pre-fix configuration class and disabling server compression made the same bundle come back uncompressed at 2.0 MB with no-store, then the shipped class and config were restored and re-verified.

Automation: MockMvc and ENV-005 already cover the core; proposed ENV-006 for the stylesheet, ENV-007 for the uncached shell and a supplemental browser-cache second-launch check.
